column1: # NOT COMMITTED. These are third-party meshes under their own licences; the
# repository does not redistribute them. scripts/fetch-corpus.sh downloads each
# from its original home into tests/corpus/files/ (gitignored) and verifies the
# checksum, so re-running is free and a truncated or upstream-changed file fails
#   filename  sha256  url  source  licence  notes
# Anything after the url column is documentation; the fetch script reads only the
# Real consumer 3D-printing files: the population Meshwright actually targets.
# Selected from the 10,000-model Thingi10K research dataset, which publishes
# per-file licence and per-file defect statistics. Every row below is CC-BY, CC0
# or public domain (NC/ND/share-alike models were excluded so the set stays usable
# if it is ever redistributed), sized 800-135,000 faces, and chosen to cover every
# v1.0 detector category across three size bands, plus clean controls. The notes
# column carries Thingi10K's own per-file measurements as key=value pairs -
# independent ground truth that CorpusGroundTruthTests checks Meshwright's
# detectors against. Research/scan rows below have no ground truth and are
# Thingiverse and Printables both refuse automated download (HTTP 403), and bulk
# fetching is against Thingiverse's terms. Hugging Face's mirror of the Thingi10K
# research dataset is how these files are reachable legitimately.
# Standard graphics/scan test meshes. Neither upstream repository carries a
# blanket licence and the models have individual provenance, so these are local
# test input only - per-model provenance needs checking before any is relied on in
# a shipped artefact or a public CI log.
